butir.teks: The generosity of ash-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) is too well known to be recounted, and the head of renunciation (zuhd) is generosity, because whoever loves something holds on to it, and none parts with wealth except one in whose eyes this world has become small, and that is the meaning of renunciation.

What indicates the strength of his renunciation, his intense fear of Allah Most High, and the preoccupation of his aspiration with the Hereafter is what is reported: that Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna related a hadith on the matters that soften the heart, and ash-Shafi'i fell unconscious. It was said to him, "He has died," and he said, "If he has died, then the best of his time has died."

And what 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Balawi related: he said, "I was sitting with 'Umar ibn Nubata, and we were discussing the worshippers and the renunciants, and 'Umar said to me, 'I have never seen anyone more scrupulous or more eloquent than Muhammad ibn Idris ash-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him). He and I and al-Harith ibn Labid went out to as-Safa. Al-Harith was a student of Salih al-Murri. He began to recite, and he had a beautiful voice, and he recited this verse to him: ⟦QS 77:35-36⟧ Then I saw ash-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) with his colour changed and his skin shivering; he trembled violently and fell down unconscious. When he recovered, he began to say, "I seek refuge in You from the standing of the liars and the turning away of the heedless. O Allah, for You the hearts of the knowers of Allah ('arifun) have humbled themselves, and the necks of those who long for You have been abased before You. My God, grant me Your generosity, cloak me with Your covering, and pardon my shortcoming by the generosity of Your Face."'"

He said, "Then he walked on and we left. When I entered Baghdad, and he was in Iraq, I sat on the riverbank to perform ablution (wudu') for the prayer, when a man passed by me and said to me, 'Young man, perfect your ablution; may Allah be good to you in this world and the Hereafter.' I turned, and there was a man followed by a group of people. I hurried in my ablution and began to follow in his footsteps. He turned to me and said, 'Do you have a need?' I said, 'Yes, teach me something of what Allah has taught you.' He said to me, 'Know that whoever is truthful to Allah is saved, whoever is apprehensive for his religion is safe from ruin, and whoever renounces this world, his eyes are cooled by what he sees of the reward of Allah Most High tomorrow. Shall I not give you more?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Whoever has three qualities has completed faith: whoever enjoins what is right and acts upon it, forbids what is wrong and refrains from it, and keeps to the limits of Allah Most High. Shall I not give you more?' I said, 'Yes, indeed.' He said, 'Be a renunciant in this world and one who desires the Hereafter, and be truthful to Allah Most High in all your affairs; you will be saved with those who are saved.' Then he went on. I asked, 'Who is this?' and they said, 'He is ash-Shafi'i.'" Now look at his falling down unconscious, then at his admonition, and how that indicates his renunciation and the utmost of his fear. This fear and renunciation are attained only through knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for ⟦QS 35:28⟧. Ash-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) did not gain this fear and renunciation from the knowledge of the Book of Salam and Ijara and the rest of the books of jurisprudence (fiqh); rather it is from the sciences of the Hereafter drawn out of the Qur'an and the reports.
For the rulings of the earlier and the later ones are lodged in the two.

As for his being knowledgeable about the secrets of the heart and the sciences of the Hereafter, you know it from the wise sayings handed down from him. It is reported that he was asked about showing off (riya'), and he said off the cuff, "Showing off is a trial that caprice (hawa) has knotted before the eyes of the hearts of the scholars; so they looked at it with the poor choice of their selves, and their deeds came to nothing."

And ash-Shafi'i (may Allah Most High have mercy on him) said, "If you fear self-admiration ('ujb) for your deed, then look at whose pleasure you seek, what reward you desire, what punishment you fear, what well-being you give thanks for, and what affliction you remember. For when you reflect on any one of these matters, your deed becomes small in your eyes." So see how he mentioned the reality of showing off and the remedy for self-admiration, and these are among the major afflictions of the heart. And ash-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "Whoever does not protect his self, his knowledge will not benefit him." And he (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "Whoever obeys Allah Most High through knowledge, his secret benefits him."

He said, "There is no one who does not have a lover and a hater; so if that is the case, be with the people of obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." It is reported that 'Abd al-Qahir ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz was a righteous and scrupulous man, and he used to ask ash-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) about questions on scrupulousness (wara'), and ash-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) would give him his attention because of his scrupulousness. One day he said to ash-Shafi'i, "Which is better: patience, trial, or empowerment (tamkin)?" Ash-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "Empowerment is the rank of the prophets, and there is no empowerment except after trial. When one is tried, he is patient, and when he is patient, he is empowered. Do you not see that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, tried Abraham (peace be upon him) and then empowered him, tried Moses (peace be upon him) and then empowered him, tried Job (peace be upon him) and then empowered him, and tried Solomon (peace be upon him) and then empowered him and gave him a kingdom? Empowerment is the best of ranks. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said, ⟦QS 12:21⟧ And Job (peace be upon him), after the great trial, was empowered. Allah Most High said, ⟦QS 21:84⟧, the verse." This speech of ash-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) indicates his deep immersion in the secrets of the Qur'an and his familiarity with the stations (maqamat) of those travelling to Allah Most High, among the prophets and the friends of Allah (awliya'); and all of that is from the sciences of the Hereafter.

And it was said to ash-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him), "When is a man a scholar?" He said, "When he has become well-grounded in the knowledge of religion and has mastered it, then turns to the rest of the sciences and looks into what he has missed; at that point he is a scholar." For it was said to Galen, "You prescribe for a single illness many combined medicines," and he said, "Only one of them is the aim, and others are put with it only to calm its sharpness, because the single one alone is deadly." This and similar things beyond counting indicate the loftiness of his rank in the knowledge of Allah Most High and the sciences of the Hereafter.

As for his seeking the Face of Allah Most High through jurisprudence and debate in it, what is related from him indicates it. He said, "I wished that people would benefit from this knowledge and that nothing of it would be ascribed to me." So see how he was aware of the affliction of knowledge and of seeking a name for it, and how his heart was kept pure from turning to it, with the intention in it purely for the Face of Allah Most High.
And ash-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "I never debated anyone and wished that he would err."

And he said, "I never spoke to anyone but I wished that he would be granted success, be guided aright, and be helped, and that he would have care and protection from Allah Most High. And I never spoke to anyone while caring whether Allah would make the truth clear on my tongue or on his." And he said, "I never presented the truth and the proof to anyone and he accepted it from me, but I held him in awe and committed myself to loving him; and no one ever contended with me arrogantly over the truth and pushed back the proof, but he fell in my eyes and I rejected him." These are the signs that indicate seeking Allah Most High through jurisprudence and debate. So see how people followed him in only one of these five qualities, and then how they opposed him even in that. For this reason Abu Thawr (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "I have never seen, and those who see have never seen, the like of ash-Shafi'i (may Allah Most High have mercy on him)."

And Ahmad ibn Hanbal (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "For forty years I have not prayed a prayer without supplicating for ash-Shafi'i (may Allah Most High have mercy on him)." So look at the fairness of the one who supplicates and the rank of the one supplicated for, and measure by him the peers and equals among the scholars of these times, and the grudge and hatred between them, so that you may know their shortcoming in claiming to follow the example of these. Because of how much he supplicated for him, his son said to him, "What kind of man was ash-Shafi'i that you supplicate for him all this supplication?" Ahmad said, "My son, ash-Shafi'i (may Allah Most High have mercy on him) was like the sun for this world and like well-being for people. So see whether there is any successor to these two." Ahmad (may Allah have mercy on him) used to say, "No one has touched an inkwell with his hand but ash-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) has a favour upon his neck."
And Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan said:

"I have not prayed a prayer for forty years without supplicating in it for ash-Shafi'i, because of the knowledge Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, opened to him and the success in rectitude He granted him in it."

Let us limit ourselves to this brief selection from his circumstances, for that lies beyond enumeration. Most of these merits we transmitted from the book that the Shaykh Nasr ibn Ibrahim al-Maqdisi (may Allah Most High have mercy on him) composed on the merits of ash-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him and with all Muslims).

As for the Imam Malik (may Allah be pleased with him), he too was adorned with these five qualities, for it was said to him, "What do you say, Malik, about seeking knowledge?" He said, "Good and beautiful; but look at what is required of you from the time you rise in the morning until you spend the evening, and hold to it." He (may Allah Most High have mercy on him) was extreme in honouring the knowledge of religion, such that when he wanted to narrate he would perform ablution (wudu'), sit at the head of his bedding, comb his beard, use perfume, and settle into his seat with dignity and gravity, and then narrate. He was asked about that, and he said, "I like to honour the hadith of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him)."

And Malik said, "Knowledge is a light that Allah places wherever He wills; it is not through abundance of narration." This respect and reverence indicates the strength of his knowledge of the majesty of Allah Most High. As for his seeking the Face of Allah Most High through knowledge, his saying indicates it: "Disputation in religion is nothing."
And what ash-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said indicates it: "I witnessed Malik when he was asked about forty-eight questions, and he said of thirty-two of them, 'I do not know.'"

Whoever seeks other than the Face of Allah Most High by his knowledge, his self is not willing to admit about itself that it does not know. For this reason ash-Shafi'i (may Allah be pleased with him) said, "When the scholars are mentioned, Malik is the piercing star, and no one has done me more favour than Malik."

It is reported that Abu Ja'far al-Mansur forbade him from narrating the hadith on the divorce of one who is coerced; then he secretly sent someone to ask him, and he narrated before a gathering of people, "There is no divorce for one who is compelled." So he flogged him with whips, yet he did not give up narrating the hadith.
And Malik (may Allah have mercy on him) said, "No man is truthful in his speech and does not lie but he is granted enjoyment of his mind, and no affliction or senility befalls him with old age."

As for his renunciation of this world, what is reported indicates it: that al-Mahdi, the Commander of the Faithful, asked him and said to him, "Do you have a house?" He said, "No, but I will tell you: I heard Rabi'a ibn Abi 'Abd ar-Rahman say, 'A man's lineage is his house.'" Ar-Rashid asked him, "Do you have a house?" and he said, "No." So he gave him three thousand dinars and said, "Buy a house with them." He took them but did not spend them. When ar-Rashid wanted to depart, he said to Malik (may Allah have mercy on him), "You should come out with us, for I have resolved to bring the people to the Muwatta' as 'Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) brought the people to the Qur'an." He said to him, "As for bringing the people to the Muwatta', there is no way to it, because the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) dispersed after him in the cities and narrated, and the people of each city have knowledge. And he (peace and blessings be upon him) said, 'The disagreement of my community is a mercy' (١). As for going out with you, there is no way to it. The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said, 'Medina is better for them if they only knew' (٢), and he (peace and blessings be upon him) said, 'Medina expels its impurity as the bellows expel the impurity of iron' (٣). And here are your dinars as they are; if you wish, take them, and if you wish, leave them." He meant that you are only burdening me with leaving Medina because of what you have bestowed on me, and I will not prefer this world over the City of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him). Such was Malik's renunciation of this world. When abundant wealth was carried to him from the ends of the world because of the spread of his knowledge and his companions, he used to distribute it among the avenues of good. His generosity indicated his renunciation and his little love for this world. Renunciation is not the absence of wealth; renunciation is the emptiness of the heart from it. Indeed, Solomon (peace be upon him), in his kingdom, was among the renunciants.

What indicates his disdain for this world is what is reported from ash-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him), that he said, "I saw at Malik's door a string of horses from the horses of Khurasan, and it is said, of Egypt, than which I had seen none finer. I said to Malik (may Allah have mercy on him), 'How beautiful it is!' and he said, 'It is a gift from me to you, Abu 'Abd Allah.' I said, 'Leave one of them for yourself, a mount you can ride.'"

He said, "I am ashamed before Allah Most High to tread with the hoof of a mount on soil in which is the Prophet of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him)." So look at his generosity, how he gave away all of that at once, and at his reverence for the soil of Medina.

What indicates his intending the Face of Allah Most High through knowledge, and his disdain for this world, is what is reported: that he said, "I went in to Harun ar-Rashid, and he said to me, 'Abu 'Abd Allah, you should come to us regularly so that our boys may hear the Muwatta' from you.' I said, 'May Allah grant honour to our lord the emir! This knowledge came out from you; if you honour it, it is honoured, and if you humiliate it, it is humiliated. Knowledge is approached; it does not approach.' He said, 'You are right. Go out to the mosque so that you may hear along with the people.'"

As for Abu Hanifa (may Allah Most High have mercy on him), he too was a worshipper, a renunciant for Allah Most High, fearful of Him, seeking the Face of Allah Most High through his knowledge. As for his being a worshipper, it is known from what is reported from Ibn al-Mubarak, who said, "Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him) had chivalry and abundant prayer."
Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman related that he used to keep the whole night alive.

It is reported that he used to keep half of the night alive. One day he passed along a road, and someone pointed at him while he was walking and said to another, "This is the one who keeps the whole night alive." After that he never ceased keeping the whole night alive. He said, "I am ashamed before Allah, glorified is He, to be described with what is not in me of worship of Him."

As for his renunciation, it is reported from ar-Rabi' ibn 'Asim, who said, "Yazid ibn 'Umar ibn Hubayra sent me, and I brought Abu Hanifa to him. He wanted him to be in charge of the public treasury, but he refused, so he flogged him twenty lashes."

So see how he fled from office and endured torment. Al-Hakam ibn Hisham ath-Thaqafi said, "I was told in Syria a report about Abu Hanifa: that he was among the most trustworthy of people, and the ruler wanted him to take charge of the keys of his treasuries or have his back flogged, so he chose their punishment of him over the punishment of Allah Most High."
It is reported that Abu Hanifa was mentioned in the presence of Ibn al-Mubarak, and he said, "Do you mention a man to whom the world was offered in its entirety and who fled from it?"

It is reported from Muhammad ibn Shuja' from some of his companions that it was said to Abu Hanifa, "The Commander of the Faithful Abu Ja'far al-Mansur has ordered ten thousand dirhams for you." He said, "Abu Hanifa was not pleased." He said, "When the day came on which it was expected that the money would be brought, he prayed the dawn prayer, then wrapped himself in his garment and did not speak. The messenger of al-Hasan ibn Qahtaba came with the money and entered upon him, but he did not speak to him. One of those present said, 'He speaks to us only a word after a word'; that is, this is his habit. He said, 'Put the money in this sack in the corner of the house.' Then Abu Hanifa afterwards left a will concerning the belongings of his house and said to his son, 'When I die and you have buried me, take this purse, go with it to al-Hasan ibn Qahtaba, and say to him, "Take your deposit that you deposited with Abu Hanifa."'"
His son said, "I did that, and al-Hasan said, 'The mercy of Allah be upon your father! He was truly miserly about his religion.'"

It is reported that he was called to the office of judge, and he said, "I am not fit for this." It was said to him, "Why?" He said, "If I am truthful, I am not fit for it; and if I am a liar, a liar is not fit for judgeship."

As for his knowledge of the way of the Hereafter and the way of the matters of religion and his knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, his intense fear of Allah Most High and his renunciation of this world indicate it. Ibn Jurayj said, "It has reached me about this Kufan of yours, Nu'man ibn Thabit, that he is intensely fearful of Allah Most High."

And Sharik an-Nakha'i said, "Abu Hanifa was long in silence, constant in reflection, and spoke little with people." This is among the clearest signs of inner knowledge and of occupation with the important matters of religion. Whoever is given silence and renunciation has been given all knowledge. This is a brief sample of the conditions of the three Imams.

As for the Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Sufyan ath-Thawri (may Allah Most High have mercy on them both), their followers are fewer than the followers of these, and Sufyan has fewer followers than Ahmad; but their fame for scrupulousness and renunciation is more evident. This whole book is filled with accounts of their deeds and sayings, so there is no need for detail now. So look now at others than these three Imams, and consider whether these states, sayings, and deeds of turning away from this world and devoting oneself wholly to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, are produced by mere knowledge of the branches of jurisprudence, namely knowing salam, ijara, zihar, ila', and li'an, or whether another knowledge, higher and nobler than it, produces them. And look at those who claimed to follow the example of these: were they truthful in their claim or not?
